$comment: THE TOWER WHOSE LIFTS ARE NOT ONE SPEED -- 20 m/s up and 10 m/s down, the first shipped building whose cars are directionally asymmetric and therefore the first on which analyzeUpPeak raises directionalSpeedAsymmetry and CLOSED_FORM_ASSUMPTIONS' symmetric-speed entry stops being a disclaimer about nothing. GitHub issue #425. THE ISSUE'S PREMISE IS STALE AND THAT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: its title says 'the car schema cannot express that', and since GitHub issue #444 landed it can -- config/schema.ts's carConfigSchema carries descentSpeedMps and cabinPressurised, physics/motion/sCurve.ts picks the top speed by the sign of the move, and #425's exit 1 (widen the schema) was therefore already taken by somebody else. What was missing was a building. NAMED IN THE REPOSITORY'S CONVENTION, burj-class-reference's: the real Guangzhou CTF Finance Centre is the reference, and the figures in this file are the project's own. PROVENANCE, per the product owner's 2026-09-08 standing ruling on governed data/ values: EVERY AUTHORED FIGURE BELOW IS AN AGENT'S PROPOSAL, drafted for the owner to accept, tighten or reject, and NOT YET APPROVED. The line the ruling asks for is drawn field by field. MEASURED (cited): the pair 20.0 / 10.0 m/s, from Hitachi's published design for this tower (1,200 m/min up, 600 m/min down, the descent limited for ear comfort rather than by the machine) -- Hitachi press release 2017-06-02 and Hitachi Review 2017 vol. 66 no. 3, both cited in GitHub issue #425. The 20.5 m/s ceiling those figures sit under is elevator-specs.json's ultra-high-speed class, whose own anchor is Shanghai Tower. CHOSEN (an agent's proposals, none of them cited, all awaiting the owner): the floor count (111 above ground, which is the published storey count) and the height ladder that realises it -- a 4.5 m office storey, a 3.5 m apartment storey and a 3.6 m hotel storey, putting the top occupied floor at 446.7 m under a 530 m roof whose spire and plant this model does not carry; the three sky lobbies at 31, 67 and 91 and the split of the tower into offices, serviced apartments and hotel over them; the populations (52 an office floor, 24 an apartment floor, 30 a hotel floor, 30 on the sky deck, 4,472 in all); the car count (36 over five banks) and every car's class, speed, rating and door; and cabinPressurised on the shuttle, whose reasoning is in that bank's own $comment and is a modelling consequence rather than a claim about the real machine. NOTHING HERE IS TAKEN FROM THE ARTICLE THAT PROMPTED #425: that is a trade-association listicle with no primary references which contradicts itself about the world's fastest lift, and the issue says in terms that it is the prompt and not the citation. WHAT THE DISTINGUISHING FEATURE BUYS, MEASURED ON THE LEGS RATHER THAN ASSERTED: packages/core/src/sim/directionalSpeedSeam.test.ts runs this building as shipped and again with descentSpeedMps deleted from the shuttle and nothing else touched, and requires the legs to differ. A restriction no generated rider needs is DECISIONS.md SS D265's defect, and the polarity that matters here is the other one: a field the shaft's own air-pressure cap would have produced anyway is a field that changes nothing, which is why this tower's shuttle is pressurised and why that decision is recorded rather than tidy. WHAT THE CLOSED FORM SAYS: the oracle is offered this building's shuttle and REFUSES it rather than reconciling, and the refusal is a throw rather than a sentence -- see packages/experiments/src/oracle/remainingBuildings.test.ts. analyzeUpPeak raises directionalSpeedAsymmetry on that bank, which no shipped bank had ever raised, and the warning says why: the published Barney/CIBSE expression has exactly one tv and charges it twice, so it has nowhere to put an asymmetry and none is invented here. WHAT THIS BUILDING IS NOT FOR: it is not in data/proof-cases.json. The owner ruled on 2026-09-10 (GitHub issues #500 and #419) that the bench's forty stay fixed so every rating stays comparable.

banks.$comment: THE ASYMMETRIC MACHINE, and the reason this bank is pressurised. CHOSEN, and every figure awaits the owner: 20.0 m/s up and 10.0 m/s down is Hitachi's published design for this tower's record lifts (1,200 m/min ascending, 600 m/min descending), read into this schema's ratedSpeedMps and descentSpeedMps. cabinPressurised is an agent's proposal and NOT a citation, and it is here for a reason worth reading before anybody 'simplifies' it away: this bank's travel is 451.2 m, above elevator-specs.json airPressure.appliesAboveTravelM (300), so an UNPRESSURISED cabin would be capped at descentCapMps (10.0) by the shaft alone -- which is the same 10.0 the machine publishes. resolveCar takes the LOWER of the two limits, so on an unpressurised arrangement deleting descentSpeedMps would change nothing at all and the authored field would be a dead seam of exactly DECISIONS.md SS D265's shape: a declared value with no consequence. Pressurising the cabin removes the shaft's cap (the airPressure block's pressurisedDescentCapMps is null, meaning no cap), so the ONLY thing holding the descent to 10.0 m/s is the machine's own published limit, and removing it moves the legs. That counterfactual is a checked-in run rather than this sentence: packages/core/src/sim/directionalSpeedSeam.test.ts.
banks.name: Sky lobby shuttle
Mid-rise office locals, off sky lobby 1

notes: Five banks and three sky lobbies, and the shuttle is the only asymmetric one. The four local banks are ordinary symmetric machines below the air-pressure threshold (139.5 m, 166.5 m, 84.0 m and 78.3 m of travel against the 300 m the shaft cap applies above), so this tower carries the asymmetry on exactly one bank and everything else in it is the model this repository already ran. That is deliberate: a building in which every car were asymmetric could not tell the reader which figures moved because of it.

The 20 m/s rating is reached on one hop and on no other, which is CLAUDE.md's 'short hops never reach rated speed' rule at the top of the catalogue. At the ultra-high-speed class's 1.2 m/s2 and 1.2 m/s3 an s-curve needs about 176.7 m to reach 20 m/s and the same again to stop, so only a run of about 353 m or more touches the plate figure: G to the sky deck is 451.2 m and does, G to sky lobby 3 is 385.5 m and does, G to sky lobby 2 is 301.5 m and does not, G to sky lobby 1 is 139.5 m and is not close. Going down the car is held at 10.0 m/s on every one of the three.

Every car states passengerTransferS, because data/buildings/README.md refuses to default one on a mixed-use building. The shuttle takes the residential 1.75 s rather than the office 1.2 s on the README's own rule -- where a bank carries more than one population the slower value is chosen, and this shuttle is the only route to the apartments and the hotel, so a guest with luggage is aboard it every trip. No new reference value is authored.
